function.name: calculate_electric_current
function.description: Calculate the electric current through a conductor given voltage and resistance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

voltage.description: The voltage across the conductor in Volts. This is a float type value.

resistance.description: The resistance of the conductor in Ohms. This is a float type value.

conductance.description: The conductance of the conductor in Siemens. Optional if resistance is provided. Default: 0.3 This is a float type value.

message.content:
Electricity wasn’t “discovered” by a single person; it was gradually uncovered by many scientists over centuries. Here’s a quick timeline of key contributors:

| Time | Contributor | Contribution |
|------|-------------|--------------|
| **6th century BCE** | **Thales of Miletus** | Noted that rubbing amber produced static charge. |
| **16th century** | **William Gilbert** | Published *De Magnete* (1600), distinguishing magnetism from static electricity and coined the term “electricity.” |
| **17th century** | **Otto von Guericke** | Demonstrated static electricity with the Leyden jar (1660). |
| **18th century** | **Benjamin Franklin** | Conducted kite experiment (1752), proposed positive/negative charges, and introduced the concept of electrical charge conservation. |
| **19th century** | **Alessandro Volta** | Invented the voltaic pile (1800), the first chemical battery. |
| **19th century** | **Michael Faraday** | Formulated Faraday’s laws of induction (1831) and discovered electromagnetic induction. |
| **19th century** | **James Clerk Maxwell** | Unified electricity and magnetism into Maxwell’s equations (1860s). |

So, while no single individual “discovered” electricity, the cumulative work of these pioneers—and many others—led to our modern understanding of electric phenomena.
